key: Three several places of his birth they honour, in mid-air, in the heaven, and in the waters. Governing in the east of earthly regions, the seasons hath he stablished in their order.
s: Early in a hymn to Agni as a newborn infant, the verse turns to his births; Sāyaṇa, on 1.95.3, reads them as the fire beneath the ocean, the sun in heaven and the lightning in mid-air, and the sun as marking off the seasons.
src: Sāyaṇa, Vedārthaprakāśa on Rig Veda 1.95.3, sa.wikisource (printed edition not named), revision 333253 (2022)

evidence.words: अस्याग्नेस्त्रीणि जन्मानि संभवन्ति । "समुद्रे अब्धौ वडवानलरूपेण “एकं जन्म । “दिवि द्युलोके आदित्यात्मना “एकम् । "अप्सु । आपः इति अन्तरिक्षनाम । अन्तरिक्षे वैद्युताग्निरूपेणैकम् । … तत्रादित्यात्मना वर्तमानः सोऽग्निः “ऋतूनु वसन्ताद्यान् षडृतून "प्रशासत् प्रकर्षेण विभक्ततया ज्ञापयन्
evidence.gloss: This Agni has three births: in the ocean, one birth, in the form of the submarine (mare’s) fire; in heaven, one, as the sun; in the waters: āpaḥ is a name of mid-air, so in mid-air, one, in the form of the lightning fire … There, abiding as the sun, that Agni makes known the seasons, the six seasons, spring and the rest, by marking them off distinctly.
evidence.licence: public domain text; transcription CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource)

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, ref 1.95.3, at [94,3]). Sāyaṇa on 1.95.3 (packet, revision 333253, dated 2022-03-02 by the Wikisource API) gives Agni’s three births: in the ocean as submarine fire (vaḍavānala), in heaven as the sun, and in the waters, which he takes as a name of mid-air, as lightning; then Agni as the sun makes known the six seasons by dividing them (prakarṣeṇa vibhaktatayā jñāpayan). The sentence carries this without drift; Wilson’s note b agrees. Plain sense: 1.95.1 to 1.95.2 present the golden Babe and Infant, Sāyaṇa names him Agni; faithful. entry-check ok.
